# Results — Study 405 (Doji Reversal) on real daily tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). One recipe — detect a doji
(real body ≤ 10% of the high-low range) on daily bars, tag the 2-day move into it, take
the **reversal** bet against that move at the next session's open, and read the forward
1 / 3 / 5 / 10-day return — pooled across a fixed basket of **SPY + 28 long-listed US
large-caps** and pinned against the **unconditional base rate** (the same against-the-move
bet on every bar). As-of **2025-12-31** (full-year cut, no partial 2026). Pooled
**n = 18,750** dojis over ~24.5 years (~26 per name per year). Panel fingerprint
`91bd864b7001`.*

> **Survivorship — named on the Signal axis.** The basket is *surviving* names (all still
> trading in 2026); a fixed surviving-names basket cannot include delisted firms. Its
> direction here is ambiguous: it does not obviously manufacture the *absence* of a doji
> effect we report.

## The honest test — doji reversal vs the unconditional base rate (gross, cost = 0)

The doji must beat the *same* against-the-prior-move bet measured on **all** bars. If it
only matches the base rate, the "reversal" belongs to generic short-horizon mean-reversion,
not to the candle.

| Horizon | n | win-rate | doji mean (bps) | HAC *t* | base rate (bps) | **doji − base** | placebo *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1 day  | 18,750 | 49.7% | −0.50 | −0.49 | +1.95 | **−2.45** | 0.995 |
| 3 days | 18,750 | 49.9% | +1.20 | +0.61 | +4.23 | **−3.03** | 0.941 |
| 5 days | 18,750 | 50.7% | **+5.98** | **+2.31** | +8.58 | **−2.60** | 0.842 |
| 10 days| 18,750 | 50.0% | +3.93 | +1.08 | +7.03 | **−3.10** | 0.812 |

- The **absolute** 5-day reversal clears the inference bar (**+5.98 bps, HAC *t* = +2.31**)
  — but that is the broad short-horizon mean-reversion, not the doji.
- The **doji − base-rate delta is negative at every horizon.** A doji is a *below-average*
  day for the reversal bet — the opposite of the folk claim.
- The **label-shuffle placebo** confirms it: a random same-size set of bars beats the dojis
  **84%** of the time at 5 days (*p* = 0.842). The doji label carries no extra information.

## Costs — net of 2 bps round-trip + 1 bp borrow on the short leg

| Horizon | gross (bps) | net (bps) |
|---|--:|--:|
| 1 day  | −0.50 | −3.00 |
| 3 days | +1.20 | −1.30 |
| 5 days | +5.98 | +3.48 |
| 10 days| +3.93 | +1.43 |

Net of friction the short horizons turn negative; the surviving 5-/10-day net is just the
base-rate bounce minus costs — there is no doji-specific gross edge to defend.

## Detector-cut robustness (h=5) — the *t* tracks sample size, not signal

| body cut φ | n | abs doji HAC *t* | doji − base (bps) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 0.05 | 9,395 | +1.29 | −3.90 |
| 0.10 | 18,764 | +2.30 | −2.62 |
| 0.15 | 28,242 | +2.53 | −3.03 |
| 0.20 | 38,009 | +3.24 | −2.45 |

A looser body cut collects more bars, lifting the absolute *t* by ≈√n — but the delta vs
base rate stays stubbornly negative. The rising *t* is an artefact, not strengthening
evidence.

## Myth-check — does a trend / volume filter rescue it? (h=5, gross)

| Filter subset | n | mean (bps) | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| Doji above 20-day SMA (uptrend) | 11,089 | −1.43 | −0.49 |
| Doji below 20-day SMA (downtrend) | 7,675 | **+16.64** | **+3.55** |
| Doji on high volume | 6,315 | +4.08 | +0.76 |
| Doji on low volume | 12,449 | +6.91 | +2.36 |

Downtrend dojis *do* bounce harder — but that is the well-known post-drop mean-reversion
that any below-average bar shows; the filter relabels the base-rate effect, it does not
isolate a doji effect. **The myth-check confirms the misattribution.**

## SPY-only sanity check (h=5, gross)

| Tape | n | mean (bps) | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| SPY | 627 | **−7.99** | −0.88 |

On the index alone the doji "reversal" is *negative* — the pooled positive number is
carried entirely by the cross-section's base-rate reversion.

## Synthetic positive control — the harness works when there's something to find

On a deterministic synthetic panel (`data.synthetic_panel`) with a *planted* doji-specific
reversal, the same harness recovers the edge; at `edge = 0` it reads ≈ 0:

| Planted edge | detected delta vs base (bps) | placebo *p* |
|---|--:|--:|
| 0.00 (null) | −1.51 | 0.716 |
| 0.01 | +19.34 | 0.000 |
| 0.02 | +38.78 | 0.000 |
| 0.04 | +84.95 | 0.000 |

The machinery is faithful: it lights up only when a real doji effect is present. The
real-tape verdict is therefore a statement about the **market**, not the method.

## Verdict

- **Signal — WEAK.** The absolute 5-day reversal clears the bar (+5.98 bps, HAC *t* =
  +2.31), but the doji-minus-base-rate delta is **negative at every horizon** (−2.60 bps at
  5 days), the label-shuffle *p* = 0.84, and the SPY-only doji is negative. The number is
  the baseline, not the doji — literature support, not a certified doji effect on this tape.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** No doji-specific gross edge; net of 2 bps + borrow the short
  horizons go negative and the rest is base-rate reversion minus friction.
- **Reversal signal? — MISATTRIBUTED.** The reversal is real but its attribution is wrong:
  it belongs to generic short-horizon mean-reversion (present on all bars and confirmed by
  the trend-filter myth-check), not to the candle of indecision.
